trace: Rubin: the separate 144-megapixel Commissioning Camera acquired test observations in late 2024. LSSTCam captured engineering images on 15 April 2025. Public First Look followed on 23 June 2025 and live science alerts by 24 February 2026. The formal survey began 29 June 2026 and was announced on 30 June. Proposed record rubin-lsst-camera covers the full instrument and its own milestones.

DECam: official first light on 12 September 2012 preceded science verification in 2012–13 and the formal DES start on 31 August 2013. Proposed record dark-energy-camera links to berkeley-fully-depleted-back-illuminated-ccd through the documented later LBNL design generation and delivery of devices for the focal plane.

Berkeley detector line: the 1996 high-resistivity silicon CCD paper explicitly cites the 1989 p-i-n detector fabrication work. A June 1988 Berkeley report already describes the p-i-n process, and a 4 December 1996 trial at Lick demonstrated the CCD on sky. The 1997 Lick-led characterization cites both publications and shares authors with the 1996 paper. Proposed berkeley-fully-depleted-back-illuminated-ccd retains a candidate link to berkeley-high-resistivity-pin-detector-process pending independent corroboration of the specific process and an established affinity to boyle-smith-charge-coupled-device-concept on their shared clocked charge-transfer principle.

The DECam instrument paper groups DECam and LSST among very large imagers. For Rubin, the technical team documents 189 science CCDs supplied by ITL and e2v and arranged in 21 rafts. Thick, fully depleted back-illuminated detectors are a shared design approach. A DECam-to-Rubin dependence link was deferred pending design-transfer evidence.
alternatives: VIRCAM used a near-infrared imaging array at Paranal and has retired. Its successor in that instrument position, 4MOST, uses optical multi-object spectroscopy. ESO documents first light, validation and readiness milestones. The 12 November 2026 consortium notice supports imminent survey operations without confirming a start.
frontier: Look for independent evidence identifying the specific 1988–89 p-i-n process as the source of the 1996 CCD fabrication method. The prototype developers' contemporary attribution is retained as a candidate link.
Check an ESO or 4MOST survey observing log for the first completed programme exposure after readiness review.
Inspect LSST sensor procurement and prototype acceptance documents to trace the installed ITL and e2v CCDs to their own prior detector generations.
screen: Searched discovery, source and lead IDs and text for CCD, charge-coupled, DECam, Rubin/LSST, VISTA, telescope and diode aliases. Existing Boyle–Smith concept includes April 1970 concept and verification publications. Existing charge-coupled-image-sensor is scoped to Fairchild CCD101 availability and kodak-sasson-digital-camera-prototype to an early Kodak system. No instrument or Berkeley detector duplicates were identified. The Kodak exact-component and consumer-access leads stay open. No shared lead was promoted.
coverage: Three sites on selected operator and participant evidence through 17 November 2026. Actual observing is documented through 12 November for Rubin and 9 November for DECam. No comprehensive Chilean instrument census, first-ever CCD priority, or Rubin vendor ancestry is claimed.
